subject: Jurisdictional egress evidence & temporary cross-border routing question
messages:
From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@medicore.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: infra@medicore.com (Sanjay Patel)
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Jurisdictional egress / temporary cross-border processing question

Olga —

Thanks for the meeting this morning. Two follow-ups from Legal & Infra: we need a concise statement of how Redwood handles temporary cross-border processing when failover or burst capacity is exercised, specifically: 

- Maximum transient egress window (hours) and whether data stays encrypted in transit and at rest when routed outside the EU.
- A roster of subprocessors that may participate in transient processing (names + countries + purpose).
- KMS/key residency: can you confirm where encryption keys reside during a failover and whether customer-managed keys (BYOK) can prevent keys from leaving the EU?
- Any operational runbook or playbook you can share that outlines the trigger conditions for cross-region failover and telemetry we can review (we mostly care about demonstrable controls).

We'd like this evidence to be attached and a one‑paragraph statement we can include in our DPA addendum. Can you also confirm timing — we'd prefer to get this within 5 business days to keep procurement moving.

Thanks,
Jamie Liu
Senior Counsel — Data Privacy
MediCore Health

P.S. Sanjay (copied) will follow up with infra-specific questions about latency and egress telemetry if needed.
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@medicore.com>
Cc: infra@medicore.com (Sanjay Patel), marissa.cole@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 12:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Jurisdictional egress / temporary cross-border processing question

Jamie —

Appreciate the clear list. TL;DR answers up front, full details and attachments below. Attaching: REDWOOD_subprocessor_roster_20270607.pdf and regional-egress-playbook_v2.docx (operational runbook).

- Transient egress window: default transient processing window is 72 hours from initial failover event. In practice we see sub-24h recovery for planned maintenance; 72h is our conservative boundary for unplanned cross-region routing.
- Encryption: all data in transit is TLS 1.3 and all at-rest copies remain encrypted. When customers use Redwood-managed keys, we rotate and store keys in KMS clusters that are regionbound by default (EU KMS, US KMS, APAC KMS). For BYOK: yes — customers can supply an EU-resident key (HSM/KMS) and we will not export that key outside the EU; in BYOK mode, neither the key material nor plaintext leaves your managed region.
- Subprocessors: roster attached; entries include the cloud provider egress nodes we use for failover, the telemetry/analytics partner (aggregated/anonymized processing), and a CDN vendor. Each entry lists the country and processing purpose.
- Runbook: the attached playbook describes trigger conditions (region outage thresholds, health-probe failures), the routing decision tree, notification cadence, and audit evidence we capture. It includes the telemetry hooks we can provide to your infra team (request/response IDs, routing timestamps, and egress region tags).

Next steps I propose: 
1) Marissa (AM) will approve providing the redacted subprocessor roster + playbook to MediCore.
2) Karthik (Infra) will confirm the final wording for the one-paragraph DPA addendum language about the 72-hour transient window and BYOK behaviour.
3) We can put the DPA addendum into DocuSign once MediCore confirms the one-paragraph language.

If you need an attestation letter signed by our security/compliance lead, we can provide that on request (standard template; 3 business day turnaround).

Attachements: REDWOOD_subprocessor_roster_20270607.pdf (redacted for non-essential PII), regional-egress-playbook_v2.docx

Cheers,

Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Security - Redwood Inference
